bibl.title: Was r Greater Than g? Evidence from Roman Egypt.
bibl.seg: Paul V. Kelly, Was r Greater Than g? Evidence from Roman Egypt.
Max Koedijk & Neville Morley (edd.), Capital in Classical Antiquity = Palgrave Studies in Ancient Economies (Cham, 2022) pp. 261-286, figg.
bibl.note: Examines whether r, the rate of return on capital, was greater than g, the rate of economic growth, in Roman Egypt. If this were the case, then, according to Piketty's model, wealth would tend to concentrate and social inequality increase. - 1. Introduction. - 2. Growth rates. - 3. Rates of return. - 4. Methodology. - 5. The housing market. - 6. The markets for land and credit. - 7. Analysis and conclusions. - Appendix: methodology and assumptions.
